body_markdown:
*Don* writes:


Hi Sajeev;


I am[circling back](https://www.hagerty.com/media/advice/piston-slap/piston-slap-sealed-or-unsealed-lexus-transfer-case/) on your advice on this transmission service. I did have this trans fluid change done by my mechanic. After 3500 miles, including a 2400-mile road trip, I feel NO difference in the seamless operation of this transmission.


In my case, the ominous warnings by others of slipping and failure due to the transmission somehow preferring old, tired fluid over fresh were unwarranted.


Thanks for your input!


*Sajeev* answers:


While I enjoy nailing a diagnosis for my readers, it’s even better when it includes debunking the[myth of lifetime fluids](https://www.hagerty.com/media/advice/piston-slap/piston-slap-ignore-automakers-service-your-transmission-before-its-too-late/) in one’s drivetrain. But my joy is tempered, because the initial question was about an LS460 AWD with enough miles (125,000) to be on the brink.


At that point, a fluid service can be a trap because worn-out fluid can be the glue holding a transmission together. It depends on an individual’s circumstances, and this vehicle doesn’t necessarily resonate with *Piston Slap* readers seeking transmission servicing advice.


(Don’s Lexus adds another wrinkle to the conversation because of its transfer case and front and rear differentials. I wasn’t too worried, as servicing these bits generally includes friction modifiers for clutch packs, if applicable.)


The risks of a fluid service on a complex component like a transmission are anything but a one-size-fits-all assessment. The components within any transmission fluid degrade differently depending on the vehicle’s:


- Mileage
- Weight
- Engine load or driving style over time
- External temperatures (over time)
- Thermal efficiency of external transmission cooler(s)
- Manufacturer fluid specifications and internal failure points


I bet there are more factors to include, and I would love to hear your thoughts in the comments below. Because a transmission service plays a critical role in keeping a vehicle alive, which means getting it wrong can cost thousands of dollars on a more rapid timeline than an owner may anticipate.


It seems like many of us are price sensitive these days, so I implore everyone reading to consider these factors before performing a transmission service. I suspect many of you need to do one to ensure years of low-cost operation, but again, this isn’t a one-size-fits-all assessment.
